summary: Re-run the failed arith-geometry lens of the RH crux team (previous attempt exceeded the 128k output-token cap) with an output-size guard, plus its 3 hostile referees

idea.lens: ARITHMETIC GEOMETRY / TRANSFER FROM WEIL (curves over F_q)
idea.title: Formal curves: an Euler-product negative control showing that no zeta-level Weil ingredient can supply the polarization; only the archimedean factor escapes
idea.crux_clause_targeted: Clause (I) A5: Weil positivity, i.e. the Hodge-index signature of the Frobenius-graph form. It is attacked at the level of which input could possibly supply it. The result sharpens the section-3 barrier ledger ("Euler product alone caps at dlVP; FE alone decides nothing; any proof must use both jointly"). In the Beurling/formal sense, "both jointly" still decides nothing, and the archimedean completion (with the integer set N) is the only zeta-level escape.

key_statements.statement: Golden fake. Over F_5, P = 1+5T+20T^2+25T^3+25T^4 is an effective formal curve (all a_d in Z>=0) with an exact FE and non-real off-line zeros. Its normalized Frobenius eigenvalues are phi^{+-1} e^{+-2pi i/3}, and Re rho = 1/2 + log(phi)/log 5 = 0.79899.
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: P = Phi_3(rT)Phi_3((5/r)T) with r = (5+sqrt5)/2 = sqrt5*phi. The a_d are exactly nonnegative up to d=30 (11, 15, 5, 190, 748, 1845, ...), and the tail argument of statement 2 covers d >= 4. N_1..N_4 = 11, 41, 26, 801; class number P(1) = 76. The Weil bound |N_k-q^k-1| <= 4q^{k/2} holds at k=1 (5 <= 8.94) and k=2 (15 <= 20). It fails at k=3 (100 > 44.7), which is an exact integer certificate of RH failure. P > 0 on R (Phi_3 factors), so all zeros are non-real. Script: fake_detail.py.

key_statements.statement: Family F(q,m) = 1+mT+(m^2-q)T^2+qmT^3+q^2T^4. For every prime power q >= 5 and integer 2sqrt(q) < m <= m*(q) (m*/q -> 2^{-1/3}), F(q,m) is effective, with a non-real off-line quartet at angles +-2pi/3. Its largest real part is Re rho_max = 1-(log 2)/(3 log q)+o(1/log q), which tends to 1.
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: s_d = c_d t_d with c_d = -1 (3 not dividing d) or 2 (3|d), and t_d = r^d+(q/r)^d a Lucas sequence. a_1 = q+1+m >= 0 and a_2 = (q^2-3q+m^2-m)/2 >= 0. The binding constraint is a_3 = (q^3-q-2m^3+6qm-m)/3 >= 0, which defines m*(q) and gives (r/q)^3 <= 1/2. For d >= 4 with 3 not dividing d, N_d >= q^d; for d >= 6 with 3|d, N_d >= q^d/2-2q^{d/2}. The Moebius tail is at most 7.5q^{d/2}, so d*a_d > 0. cube_family.py: the valid m form one contiguous range up to m*; m*/q -> 0.794 and (1-beta_max)log q -> 0.2310 = (log 2)/3.

key_statements.statement: Census: the zeta-level axioms leave mostly fakes. Genus 1 (q >= 5): the curve is effective iff |a| <= q, and satisfies RH iff |a| <= 2sqrt(q). So Euler product + exact FE + effectivity give only |alpha| < q, the analogue of the trivial zero-free region. Genus 2, q = 25: 1369 RH-true curves against 14828 real and 22046 non-real fakes.
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: a_2 = (q^2+q-a^2+a)/2 excludes a = -(q+1); a = q+1 is the degenerate Z = 1. Small d are checked exactly; large d follow by dominance with |alpha| < q-1. Verified for q in {5,...,101}: 2*floor(2sqrt q)+1 RH-true and 2(q-floor(2sqrt q)) fakes. Genus-2 exhaustive box scans in genus2_scan.py.

key_statements.statement: Zeta-level completeness. Every formal curve with separable characteristic polynomial chi carries: an integral Frobenius lattice with a nondegenerate q-symplectic form; the Rosati involution F' = qF^{-1}; an effective formal square; formal Lefschetz intersection numbers; and an exact radical (P(F) in the kernel of the window-2g Toeplitz form). RH holds iff the Rosati trace form Tr(xx') on Q[F] is positive definite. So the polarization is the unique missing Weil ingredient, and the rest do not imply it.
key_statements.status: THEOREM-paper-proof (standard constructions; verified numerically on examples)
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: The symplectic form is omega(u,v) = Tr(lambda u iota(v)) with iota(x) = q/x and iota(lambda) = -lambda. N_d^2 is a Dold sequence (product of ghost coordinates in the big Witt ring), and a_d(square) >= 0 by dominance (checked to d=30). Formal Cayley-Hamilton gives ||T_4 P|| = 4e-15 for F(5,5). Tr(xx') = sum_i x(alpha_i)x(q/alpha_i) is positive definite iff q/alpha_i = conj(alpha_i) for all i.

key_statements.statement: Barrier III. Consider the class of all xi = G*E that are entire, of order <= 1, self-dual and real on the critical line, where E is a Beurling Euler product with nonnegative integer exponents and exact integer counting. No criterion whose hypotheses hold throughout this class can prove RH, or any zero-free strip Re s < 1-delta. So the program's rule 'Euler + FE jointly' is necessary but not sufficient.
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: F(5,5) belongs to the class and violates RH with non-real zeros. The members F(q,m*) have non-real zeros with real part tending to 1. DH is not in the class (it has no Euler product), so Barrier III strictly extends Barriers I and II. Kernel-checkable in the same way as FEBarrier.fe_uniform_criterion_is_false.

key_statements.statement: Periodicity obstruction. No Beurling system with all norms in q^Z, in particular no formal curve, admits a self-dual completion by pi^{-s/2}Gamma(s/2). So Barrier III spares exactly the arguments that consume the archimedean Gamma factor or the integer set N (Hamburger).
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: Z(s) is periodic with period 2pi i/log q, so Z(1-s)/Z(s) is periodic. Self-duality would force G(s)/G(1-s) = pi^{1/2-s}Gamma(s/2)/Gamma((1-s)/2) to be periodic too. But it has a pole at s = 0 and none at 2pi i/log q, a contradiction.

key_statements.statement: Connes-strategy corollary. For formal curves violating RH, the window-2g form has the numerator in its kernel (an exact radical) yet is indefinite. Its minimal-eigenvector (Caratheodory-Fejer) approximants lie on the circle but are not the zeros. Hence the step 'approximants converge to the zeros' in arXiv:2602.04022 cannot follow from Euler product + FE + radical structure; it must consume the polarization.
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: F(5,5), window 4: eigenvalues -8.22, -2.36, 0, 10.22, 20.36. The minimal eigenvector's roots have |z| = 1 and arguments +-0.6725pi and +-0.1768pi. The true zeros have |z| = phi^{+-1} and arguments +-2pi/3. Indefiniteness comes from the rank-2 pair form 2Re[p(z)conj p(1/conj z)]. This strengthens the zeta/DH version run by the crux-lee-yang lens with an Euler product.

key_statements.statement: Beurling-Hamburger rigidity: a Beurling system whose zeta satisfies the exact Riemann FE (poles only at 0 and 1, finite order) is the ordinary integers. If true, over Q the archimedean completion eliminates every fake that the geometric polarization has to exclude over F_q. That would make the archimedean factor the only zeta-level candidate to replace Weil's positivity.
key_statements.status: CONJECTURE (route identified, not verified); the consequence is HEURISTIC
key_statements.proof_sketch_or_evidence: The FE is equivalent to self-duality of nu = c*delta_0 + sum_{n in N}(delta_n + delta_{-n}) (Bochner; Hilberdink-Lapidus Thm 3.2). If N is uniformly discrete, Lev-Olevskii (Invent. 200, 2015) puts supp(nu) in finitely many cosets of a lattice. It remains to show that the residues of a multiplicative semigroup modulo a lattice force integral primes; Hamburger then gives zeta. Consistent with Kaczorowski-Perelli degree-1 rigidity.

idea.load_bearing_step:
The load-bearing step is effectivity of F(q,m) for ALL d: the fakes must be honest Euler products with nonnegative integer exponents; everything else is soft.
- Binding case d = 3: a_3 = (q^3-q-2m^3+6qm-m)/3 >= 0 defines m*(q) and yields (r/q)^3 <= 1/2.
- Cases d <= 2 are explicit.
- For d >= 4, a dominance bound applies: N_d >= q^d when 3 does not divide d, and N_d >= q^d/2-2q^{d/2} when 3|d. The Moebius tail is at most 7.5q^{d/2}.
The second load-bearing step is the periodicity delimitation. Without it, Barrier III would be overclaimed as refuting all Euler+FE arguments for zeta; in fact it refutes only those that do not consume Gamma(s/2) or the integer set N.
idea.dh_negative_control:
Formal curves complement DH; they are not subsumed by it.
- DH has the archimedean Gamma((s+1)/2) and a conductor-5 FE, but no Euler product.
- Formal curves have a genuine Euler product (nonnegative integer multiplicities, prime-power support, an effective formal square), but no archimedean factor.
Barrier I (DH) and Barrier III (fakes) together force any valid proof to consume the Euler product AND the archimedean Gamma factor (or the integer set N) jointly. Zeta and Selberg-class L-functions have both, and no known object with both violates RH. This construction uses arithmetic in a way DH cannot: it is an Euler-product-carrying negative control, so it tests exactly the Euler-product-using arguments that DH cannot test. The idea does not claim to prove positivity, so there is no zeta argument for DH to break. It does predict that any future positivity argument that is uniform over formal curves is false.
idea.circularity_check:
No statement is RH-equivalent.
- All theorems concern auxiliary formal curves and are proved by exact integer arithmetic plus a tail bound.
- The periodicity obstruction is an elementary argument about where poles sit.
- Beurling-Hamburger rigidity is logically independent of RH: it would identify the class, not locate zeros.
Against the dossier tests: (a) not a relabeling; (b) the control explicitly carries an Euler product; (c) it is a class-level barrier, not a finite-height or small-width certificate; (d) not applicable. The only non-theorem claim (the archimedean place is the unique candidate polarization) is tagged HEURISTIC and is used in no proof. conjecture1_proved = False.
idea.literature_nearest: Weil 1948 and Bombieri, Bourbaki 430 (the Castelnuovo route). Honda-Tate/Waterhouse (which Weil polynomials occur). Serre, Rational Points on Curves over Finite Fields (2020): explicit formula, Oesterle bounds. Knopfmacher, arithmetical semigroups. Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer 2006 and Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas arXiv:2004.11501 (Beurling systems without FE; the dlVP ceiling). Hamburger 1921, Bochner, and Hilberdink-Lapidus math/0410270 (Beurling FE equivalent to a theta identity). Lev-Olevskii, Invent. 200 (2015). Kaczorowski-Perelli (degree-1 Selberg class). Connes arXiv:2602.04022 (Letter-to-Riemann strategy; Connes-van Suijlekom Thm 6.1). Connes-Consani 1502.05580 (square of the arithmetic site). Kurokawa/Akatsuka/Tanaka arXiv:2008.07752 (absolute tensor squares). Deninger arXiv:2204.02714 (no real-coefficient Weil cohomology). Program docs RH_F1_* and RH_BARRIER_FE_UNIFORMITY_DESIGN (Barriers I-II). The existence of effective non-Weil zeta functions is folklore-level. New here: the explicit non-real family with Re rho -> 1, the zeta-level completeness list, the periodicity delimitation, and the use as a class-level Euler-product negative control that upgrades the program's barrier ledger.

refs.reason:
CIRCULARITY / RELABELING VERDICT: no kill. No statement is used as a proof route to RH, and none of the load-bearing claims is a zeta RH-equivalent. conjecture1_proved = False is respected throughout. There is one tautology, which I flag below; it is harmless because nothing downstream uses it.

INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION (my own exact-integer script, not the author's):
- F(5,5) checks out. N_1..N_4 = 11, 41, 26, 801. a_1..a_7 = 11, 15, 5, 190, 748, 1845, 12320, and min a_d = 5 for d <= 60. P(1) = 76. Re rho = 0.798994. The Weil bound holds at k=1 (5 <= 8.94) and k=2 (15 <= 20) and fails at k=3 (100 > 44.72). The factorization Phi_3(rT)Phi_3((q/r)T) checks coefficient by coefficient.
- Cube family. For q in {5,7,8,9,11,13,16,25,27,49,101,1009}, the effective m form one contiguous range from floor(2 sqrt q)+1 up to m*. m*/q = 0.795 at q=1009, and (1-beta_max)log q = 0.2312 at q=1009, which approaches (log 2)/3 = 0.2310. The claims hold.
- Genus 1. For q in {5,7,11,25}, effectivity holds exactly for -q <= a <= q+1, where a = q+1 is the degenerate Z = 1. This matches the census.
- The Toeplitz min-eigenvalue output of fake_detail.py runs and shows indefiniteness. I did not independently re-derive the -8.22 figure or the Caratheodory-Fejer node angles.

ISSUES (correctness and overclaim, not circularity):

1. The headline family is superseded by genus 1. Barrier III's zero-free-strip clause needs zeros with Re rho -> 1. Genus 1 with a = q already gives Re rho = log((q+sqrt(q^2-4q))/2)/log q, which is about 1 - 1/(q log q). That converges to 1 much faster than the cube family's 1 - (log 2)/(3 log q), and its effectivity proof is simpler. "Non-real zeros" is a T-plane (Frobenius-eigenvalue) distinction only. In the s-plane every fake is 2 pi i/log q periodic, so the genus-1 Siegel-type real zero also has non-real off-line translates. The cube family adds a pretty example (the golden fake) and non-real Frobenius angles. It is not load-bearing for Barrier III. Calling it the "main construction" and its effectivity the "load-bearing step" is misplaced emphasis.

2. Statement 4 is a tautology dressed as a finding. "Polarization is the unique missing ingredient" and "RH iff the Rosati trace form is positive definite" together are Weil's standard two-line equivalence: Tr(x x') is positive definite iff q/alpha = conj(alpha) for all alpha. Once fakes exist, any RH-equivalent property is "the missing ingredient", and uniqueness is not a theorem. The statement is correct but should be retagged as a standard equivalence (Weil), not a result.

3. The delimitation (statement 6) is correct but overclaimed. The periodicity argument is valid: the Gamma ratio has a pole at s = 0 and none at 2 pi i/log q, while Z(1-s)/Z(s) is periodic. But "Barrier III spares EXACTLY arguments consuming Gamma(s/2) or N" is false as stated. Any argument that uses a non-periodic feature also escapes: the single pole at s = 1 (fakes have poles at 1 + 2 pi i k/log q), zero density N(T) ~ (T/2pi)log T (fakes have linear density), or polynomial vertical growth. The escape set is "anything non-periodic", which is far larger. The phrasing should be downgraded to "spares at least".

4. Barrier III is logically valid (modus tollens) but narrow. It is also partly folklore: effective non-Weil zeta functions and the effectivity-versus-RH split appear in the Serre/Oesterle explicit-formula and linear-programming literature and in Tsfasman-Vladut. No serious existing RH approach has hypotheses that hold uniformly over q-periodic systems, so the practical content is a ledger upgrade ("Euler + FE jointly" is not sufficient), not a refutation of any live strategy. The real, sharper open question is whether a NON-periodic Beurling system with FE and an archimedean factor can violate RH. That is the conjecture, which the idea leaves unaddressed.

5. Statement 7 (Connes corollary) overreaches. It shows that the approximant-convergence step cannot follow from Euler product + FE + radical uniformly over formal curves. "It must consume the polarization" has no meaning over Q, where no polarization is known. What it must consume is something that the fakes lack, for example non-periodicity or the archimedean place.

6. Beurling-Hamburger rigidity (statement 8) may already be known in whole or in part. Before it is called new, check it against the Hamburger-type theorems for generalized Dirichlet series sum a_n lambda_n^{-s} with the Riemann FE (Bochner 1951/1958; Chandrasekharan-Mandelbrojt, Ann. Math. 1957) and the Kaczorowski-Perelli work on Hamburger's theorem. If those already force lambda_n = cn, the conjecture reduces to adding multiplicativity and may be close to known. The proposed Lev-Olevskii route also assumes uniform discreteness, which Beurling systems need not have. It is correctly tagged CONJECTURE.

CHECKS AGAINST THE TWO CLASSIC DEATHS:
(1) Circularity: none. The Rosati tautology stays within formal curves and is used in no proof.
(2) Negative control: not applicable in the usual sense. The idea is itself a negative control that carries an Euler product, and it correctly notes that DH cannot play this role.

NET: correct, honestly tagged, and elementary. Novelty is modest (an explicit non-real family, the periodicity delimitation, the ledger framing), and the headline family is dominated by genus 1 for the barrier's purpose.
refs.salvage:
Keep it as a barrier-ledger entry and a kernel-checkable artifact, with these corrections:

1. Reorder the evidence. State Barrier III with the genus-1 witness (a = q; effectivity iff -q <= a <= q; Re rho = log((q+sqrt(q^2-4q))/2)/log q, which tends to 1) as the primary zero-free-strip refutation. It is simpler and converges faster. Keep F(5,5) and F(q,m) as the witness with non-real Frobenius eigenvalues and as the concrete Connes/Toeplitz counterexample. Say explicitly that "non-real" is a statement about Frobenius eigenvalues, because in the s-plane every fake has non-real off-line zeros by periodicity.

2. Retag statement 4. "RH iff the Rosati form is positive definite" becomes "standard equivalence (Weil)". Drop "unique missing ingredient", or rephrase it as: the listed zeta-level ingredients do not imply polarization positivity (witness F(5,5)).

3. Weaken the delimitation. Change "spares exactly arguments that consume Gamma(s/2) or N" to "spares every argument that uses a non-periodic feature: the archimedean Gamma factor, a single pole at s=1, T log T zero density, polynomial vertical growth, or the integer norm set". Keep the periodicity theorem itself; it is correct and short.

4. Weaken the Connes corollary. Change "must consume the polarization" to "must consume an input that fails for q-periodic Euler products (non-periodicity or archimedean data)". Before citing -8.22 and the node angles, re-derive them independently with an explicitly stated Toeplitz/Frobenius-graph form definition.

5. Treat the conjecture as the real frontier, after a literature check. Before calling Beurling-Hamburger rigidity new, check Bochner (1951, 1958), Chandrasekharan-Mandelbrojt (Ann. Math. 1957) and Kaczorowski-Perelli on Hamburger for generalized Dirichlet series. If rigidity for general lambda_n with the Riemann FE is already known, the new content is the multiplicative (Beurling) specialization plus its interpretation. Also note that the Lev-Olevskii step needs uniform discreteness, which Beurling norm sets need not have. The most valuable next question: does any non-periodic Beurling system (FE with Gamma factor, or even FE only) exist that violates RH? A positive answer would give a genuinely strong Barrier IV. A negative answer would make "the archimedean place is the only zeta-level escape" a theorem rather than a HEURISTIC.

6. Buildable now, and worth building. FormalCurveControl emitter: self-reciprocity, a_d >= 0 via the Lucas recurrence up to d=30 plus the tail lemma, the exact violation certificate (N_3-q^3-1)^2 > 4g^2 q^3 (for F(5,5): 10000 > 2000, by decide), and the integral q-symplectic identity C^T omega C = q omega. Pair it with FormalCurveBarrier.lean mirroring FEBarrier.fe_uniform_criterion_is_false, and include the genus-1 witness family as the simplest instance. Status: kernel-checkable THEOREMs about auxiliary objects only. conjecture1_proved = False.

refs.reason:
NEGATIVE-CONTROL REFEREE: PASS, but only because the idea makes no claim about zeta. I checked the numbers myself in /private/tmp/claude-0/crux-arith-geometry/ref/chk.py; nothing here depends on the author's scripts.

What checks out:
- F(5,5): N_1..N_4 = 11, 41, 26, 801. The a_d start 11, 15, 5, 190, 748, 1845, ... and all 40 checked are nonnegative integers. P(1) = 76. The Weil bound holds at k = 1 (5 <= 8.94) and k = 2 (15 <= 20) and fails at k = 3 (100 > 44.7). The T-roots have |z| = phi^2 and phi^{-2}, which gives Re rho = 0.79899 and 0.20101.
- Family F(q,m): effective for a single contiguous range of m for q in {5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13, 16, 25, 27, 49, 101, 125, 127}. m*/q settles near 0.80, and Re rho_max rises monotonically toward 1 (0.952 at q = 127). This matches the (r/q)^3 <= 1/2 analysis.
- The periodicity obstruction is correct and elementary. The Gamma ratio has a pole at s = 0 and none at 2 pi i/log q.

Walk on Davenport-Heilbronn / Epstein. The construction is itself a negative control and makes no positive zeta argument, so there is no step that could "go through" on DH. The test passes vacuously. The real question is whether it adds anything DH and Epstein do not. It adds one thing: a control that has an Euler product. That is its only real contribution.

Hostile points (these limit the value; none is a kill):
1. RELABELING in Consequence 1 / statement 4. "RH iff the Rosati trace form Tr(x x') on Q[F] is positive definite" is RH restated. Positivity holds iff conj(alpha) = q/alpha for every alpha, which is |alpha| = sqrt q. "The polarization is the unique missing ingredient" is therefore a definition, not a finding. The only content is "fakes exist". The "zeta-level completeness" list is also stacked:
   - The "exact radical" (P(F) in the kernel of the window-2g Toeplitz form of power sums) is linear-recurrence / Cayley-Hamilton. It holds for ANY 2g numbers, off-line or not.
   - The q-symplectic form and the formal square are just as automatic.
   - "Unique missing" also ignores other missing items, for example being realized as the H^1 of an actual curve. Honda-Tate plus the curve-realization problem is the true dividing line, not Rosati alone.
2. Barrier III has a narrow scope. The class allows ARBITRARY entire order-1 completions G. The program's rule "Euler + FE jointly" always meant zeta's own FE with pi^{-s/2}Gamma(s/2), and statement 6 proves that no formal curve can have that. So Barrier III refutes only criteria that never use the Gamma factor or the integer set N. Every serious zeta strategy uses them: Weil explicit formula with the archimedean term, Connes' prolate / archimedean Weil form, de Branges, Li with the Gamma contribution. The barrier is real but hits few live targets. Its honest statement is "the archimedean place is load-bearing", and that is already the working consensus behind Connes-Consani.
3. The Connes corollary attacks a straw man. Connes' 2602.04022 convergence step is built on the archimedean Weil form (prolate operators). It is not uniform over (Euler product + FE + radical). A fake that breaks a uniform version says nothing about the actual step.
4. Novelty is thin. Effective non-Weil "virtual zeta functions" over F_q are folklore:
   - the linear-programming / explicit-formula literature (Serre, Oesterle, Tsfasman-Vladut) needs RH as a separate input because a_d >= 0 does not imply it;
   - Epstein and DH already killed "FE is enough";
   - "Euler product + FE + Ramanujan implies RH" is exactly Selberg-class GRH, which is open and has no counterexample, so the "prediction" in the DH-control section restates a known conjecture.
   New are the explicit non-real family with Re rho -> 1 at rate (log 2)/(3 log q), the golden fake, and the ledger upgrade. That is modest but correct, and cheap to kernel-check.
5. The Beurling-Hamburger "conjecture" may already be known. Generalized Hamburger theorems for general Dirichlet series sum a_n lambda_n^{-s} with Riemann's Gamma(s/2) FE are classical (Bochner 1951, "Some properties of modular relations"; Chandrasekharan-Mandelbrojt 1957, "On Riemann's functional equation"). I believe they force lambda_n = n and the function to be c*zeta under mild growth conditions; this is my recollection and I did not re-read the papers. A Beurling system with the Riemann FE is the self-dual special case. Check this before calling it a CONJECTURE: it may be a THEOREM-literature. The Lev-Olevskii route is also incomplete, because Beurling N need not be uniformly discrete.

No circularity in the main theorems. The mathematics is verified. The DH/Epstein control is not applicable, so there is nothing to fail. Not a kill, but the content sits well away from the crux.

VERDICT: keep, low value (3/10). The math is correct and the key numbers check out. As a pure-math contribution it is mostly folklore. Its real use is as a cheap, kernel-checkable negative control for the program's barrier ledger. conjecture1_proved = False; nothing here touches RH.

WHAT I RE-CHECKED (exact integer arithmetic, independent of the author's scripts):
- F(5,5): P = 1+5T+20T^2+25T^3+25T^4 is self-reciprocal (q^2 T^4 P(1/(5T)) = P).
- Using the Lucas recurrence t_d = 5t_{d-1} - 5t_{d-2}, I get N_1..N_5 = 11, 41, 26, 801, 3751.
- a_1..a_8 = 11, 15, 5, 190, 748, 1845, 12320, 52400. All a_d for d <= 39 are nonnegative integers.
- Class number P(1) = 76.
- RH-violation certificate: (N_3 - q^3 - 1)^2 = 10000 > 4g^2 q^3 = 2000.
The golden fake is real. The tail argument for d >= 4 (N_d >= q^d, or >= q^d/2 - 2q^{d/2} when 3|d, against a Moebius tail of at most 7.5q^{d/2}) is routine and believable. "RH iff the Rosati trace form is positive definite" is textbook algebra: q/alpha = conj(alpha) iff |alpha|^2 = q. The periodicity obstruction is correct and elementary.

CIRCULARITY / NEGATIVE CONTROL: Both pass trivially. The idea is itself a negative control and claims nothing about zeta, so there is nothing to relabel and nothing for DH to break. It does usefully complement DH: DH has the archimedean factor but no Euler product; formal curves have the Euler product but no archimedean factor.

NOVELTY (why the score is low):
1. The core message is folklore. "Euler product + FE + integrality do not imply RH over F_q; only the geometry (Castelnuovo/Hodge index on C x C) does" is the standard lesson of Weil's proof. Effective zeta-like functions that fail RH are known in several places: additive arithmetical semigroups (Knopfmacher Axiom A#, Zhang Wen-Bin), Beurling systems with zeros approaching Re s = 1 (Diamond-Montgomery-Vorhauer 2006; Broucke-Debruyne-Vindas), and the Tsfasman-Vladut / Lachaud-Tsfasman literature on "virtual" zeta functions, where RH is imposed as a separate axiom. The genuinely new pieces are small: the explicit non-real cube family F(q,m), the value m*/q -> 2^{-1/3} with Re rho_max -> 1, the golden fake, and the packaging as "Barrier III".
2. Barrier III spares every serious approach. The idea's own periodicity theorem shows formal curves cannot carry pi^{-s/2}Gamma(s/2). So Barrier III refutes only criteria that never touch the archimedean place. Weil's explicit formula, the Connes/Connes-Consani programs (Sonin space, archimedean Weil positivity) and Li/Keiper-type criteria all consume the Gamma factor, so none of them is refuted. Statement 5 (the Connes corollary) is correct but expected. The convergence step in arXiv:2602.04022 is essentially RH-strength, so nobody expected it to follow from Euler product + FE + radical. The -8.22 eigenvalue and the misplaced Caratheodory-Fejer nodes are a nice concrete illustration, not a new obstruction.
3. The "next target" is probably already known. Beurling-Hamburger rigidity looks like a direct corollary of classical results: Hamburger's theorem for general Dirichlet series with arbitrary exponents lambda_n (Bochner 1951; Bochner-Chandrasekharan, Ann. Math. 63 (1956) 336-360; Chandrasekharan-Mandelbrojt). Those results give uniqueness for Riemann's FE with finitely many poles, and uniqueness forces lambda_n = n. Beurling multiplicativity then forces the ordinary integers. The Lev-Olevskii route is then unnecessary. Knopp (Invent. Math. 117 (1994) 361-372) shows that uniqueness fails once you allow infinitely many poles, which pins down the right hypotheses. CAVEAT: my web-search budget ran out before I could confirm the exact statement of Bochner-Chandrasekharan; this attribution is from memory. Either way, the claim should not go out as a new conjecture until it has been checked against those papers.
4. The heuristic "the archimedean place is the unique zeta-level replacement for Weil's polarization" is the standard folklore reading (Connes, Deninger, Haran). It is correctly tagged HEURISTIC, but it is not new insight.

STATUS-TAG AUDIT:
- Statements 1, 2, 4, 6: honest.
- Statement 3: honest as tagged (the genus-2 proportions are CONJECTURE-with-evidence).
- Statement 5 (Barrier III): valid, but it holds only for criteria uniform over an arbitrary gamma factor G. Every mention must carry that qualifier, or it overclaims.
- Statement 7: CONJECTURE tag is likely wrong; it is probably a known theorem (see point 3).

LEAN 4 / MATHLIB BUILDABILITY: Yes, today, at modest cost. Self-reciprocity, a_d for d <= 30, and the violation certificate go through decide/norm_num on integers. Remember the footgun that Rat does not kernel-reduce: use Z and cast. The integral q-symplectic identity C^T omega C = q omega is a 4x4 decide. The tail lemma for all d needs a real-analysis bound on the Lucas sequence. Tractable, but it is the only nontrivial proof work. FormalCurveBarrier.lean can mirror FEBarrier.fe_uniform_criterion_is_false directly. Non-real zeros: a rational SOS certificate that P > 0 on R works. So does the observation that r is irrational and P has no real roots, and the violation alone already suffices for "not RH".

Sources consulted: local NOTES.md, fake_detail.py, hilberdink.txt (Hilberdink-Lapidus, math/0410270); web: Knopp, Invent. Math. 117 (1994) (eudml.org/doc/144219); Knopp, "Hamburger's Theorem on zeta(s) and the Abundance Principle" (link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-0348-7023-8_12); Bochner-Chandrasekharan, Ann.
